subject: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Thompson <jamal.thompson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 18:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps

Hi Jamal / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can keep momentum: 

• Economic buyer: Jamal Thompson (VP Product) — primary sign-off for value / ROI.
• Security / Legal: Priya Singh — expect security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence request.
• Procurement: procurement@acmecorp.com — will handle contracting/PO, standard timeline ~3–4 weeks once SOW and pricing are agreed.
• Decision criteria called out on the call: production latency (p95), predictable unit cost, and private deployment options for regulated data.

Agreed next steps (action owners):
1) I’ll send a draft mutual action plan (MAP) and a first-pass commercial summary — attached: Acme-MAP-draft.xlsx, deal-summary.pdf.
2) Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team (Lukas) — propose next Wed/Thu.
3) Security: provide SOC2 summary and answer initial questionnaire items — attaching SOC2-summary.pdf.
4) Procurement: confirm whether you require a standard PO or DocuSign, and any baseline contract terms that are non-negotiable (e.g., payment terms, data residency).

Two items flagged on the call that may require internal exception requests on our side:
- Acme requested a 30% one-time discount tied to first-year committed usage.
- They requested a 99.9% SLA with a specific SLA credit schedule and some contract redlines around indemnity.

If that’s accurate, Jamal — can you confirm the stakeholder list and procurement timeline? Priya — any immediate red flags on the security asks?

I’ve CC’d Aditya (revenue/discount approvals) and Lukas (technical) so we can align internally.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: Acme-MAP-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf), deal-summary.pdf (pdf)
From: Jamal Thompson <jamal.thompson@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps

Thanks for the note — that matches our view. A couple clarifications: 

• Stakeholders: correct on Jamal (me) as economic buyer, Priya as security, procurement (cc’d) will own contracting. I’ll also loop in finance if we get to MSA/ordering.
• Timeline: procurement currently has a 3–4 week process but if there are exceptions this can extend. We’re aiming to be live in Q2.

On pricing / SLA: we’re going to push for a 30% discount off list for Y1 if we commit to 12 months, and we need a 99.9% SLA with standard crediting. Also want clarifications on data residency and the private deployment option you mentioned.

Priya — any immediate security blockers or should we proceed to share the questionnaire?

—Jamal
Jamal Thompson
VP, Product — Acme Corp
jamal.thompson@acmecorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps — approval request (discount / SLA)

Folks — forwarding Jamal’s reply (below). Acme is asking for: 30% Y1 discount and a 99.9% SLA with specific crediting. They’ll also require SOC2 artifacts and potentially contract redlines on indemnity and data residency.

High-level deal metrics: 
• Estimated ARR (year 1 committed): $420k
• ACV expected: $420k
• Strategic rationale: large reference account in e-commerce vertical, high technical profile, likely to expand into additional products if initial rollout succeeds.

Request: I need approval to pursue a buying-process exception for the following items so we can keep the procurement timeline tight: 
1) Pricing exception — one-time 30% off list for Y1 (they commit to 12 months).
2) SLA exception — accept 99.9% availability target with our standard SLA credit but allow one commercial-credit bucket exception and limited indemnity redline concessions (legal review required).

Trade-offs I propose if we approve: 
• Limit the discount to Year 1 only, revert to list in Year 2.
• Require a minimum committed usage clause in the SOW.
• Require Legal + Finance sign-off on any SLA redlines before signature.

Attachments: deal-summary.pdf (financials and rationale)

Can you confirm approvals (or conditions) by EOD tomorrow so I can respond to Jamal and keep the momentum with procurement?

Thanks —
Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps — approval request (discount / SLA)

Marissa — thanks for the context and the economics. I’m comfortable approving a commercial exception but with conditions: 

1) Discount: approve up to 25% for Year 1 (not 30%). Anything >25% requires explicit VP revenue approval. We should structure it as a one-time onboarding credit spread across the first 3 invoices.
2) SLA: Legal must review redlines — we will not agree to unlimited indemnity or data residency obligations that require on-prem. We can accept a 99.9% target but cap financial exposure and require an SLA carve-out for force majeure and scheduled maintenance.
3) Procurement exceptions: require that procurement accepts a minimum committed usage clause and a defined termination period with 30 days notice after Year 1.

Please get Legal in the loop (I’ll flag with them after you confirm). If Acme insists on 30% we should push for a longer commitment term (24 months) or additional product seats as compensation.

Aditya
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamal Thompson <jamal.thompson@acmecorp.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@priya.singh@acmecorp.com>, procurement@acmecorp.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap & procurement next steps — proposed commercial path

Jamal / Priya / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick responses and for confirming stakeholders. We had an internal review with Revenue Ops and can propose the following commercial path to keep the procurement window tight: 

1) Pricing: Redwood can offer a one-time 25% discount on list for Year 1 (applies to committed usage; credit applied across the first three invoices). We cannot stretch to 30% without extended commitment — if Acme prefers 30% we’d need a 24-month commit or additional seats.

2) SLA: We can commit to a 99.9% target. Our Legal team will provide an SLA addendum with capped remedies and a standard carve-out for scheduled maintenance/force majeure. We’ll require contract redline review but are willing to accept limited indemnity adjustments; anything material will need Legal sign-off. Attached is our Redwood-SLA-exception-form.pdf for tracking required concessions.

3) Security & procurement: attaching SOC2-summary.pdf and we’ll complete the questionnaire. If procurement prefers DocuSign, send over the template and we’ll route to Legal/Finance. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567.

Next steps: 
• Jamal — please confirm you can accept a 25% Y1 credit and whether Acme will sign a 12mo or 24mo commit.
• Procurement — please share the contract template or confirm PO vs DocuSign flow.
• Priya — we’ll send the questionnaire; any high-priority security asks let us know so we can prioritize responses.

We appreciate the partnership — aiming to keep this Q2.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: Redwood-SLA-exception-form.pdf (pdf), SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)
